categories.name: Falls and fear of falling

notes: Counts computed by script from _working/candidates/*.json after the independent check was applied (see check_applied); origin was not used. Total 200; allocations range 7 to 12 (C01 fixed at 11 and unchanged). Audience: practitioners 77 (38.5%), public 68 (34.0%), both 55 (27.5%). Every category has at least a quarter public-primary posts (C16 and C18 exactly 25%), so none is claimed as inherently professional. Every series has at least 14 posts (lowest: Who gets left out 15 after C16-03 was replaced by C16-18; Weighing it up 17, What gets counted 17). Only 11 posts (5.5%) are criticism; 142 (71.0%) teach, explain, support a decision or show good care. Within-category clusters are held to two or fewer (e.g. CFS C05-16/24; prognosis C19-17/18; dying at home C19-04/10; knee and hip arthritis C10-30/16; urine infection C12-17/23; sleeping tablets C11-16/03). Reserves follow max(3, ceil(allocation/4)) except C01 (4, fixed). Every category where losing one public post would take it below a quarter now has a public-primary reserve, except C17: C17 has no suitable public reserve (the other public candidates rest on gov.uk benefit pages or repeat C03-12 or C03-09), so C17-07 is written on Schulz 2004 with the money rules optional; if a C17 public post still fails, record C17 as below a quarter public rather than inherently professional. The same applies to C18 if both C18-15 and C18-22 fail. HOW TO USE RESERVES: write the selected posts; promote a reserve only when research marks a selected post 'drop', using the category's 'fallbacks' map where it names one, otherwise the first reserve of the same audience. Do not let a reserve displace a selected post because it has a higher judge score: several reserves outrank selected posts (e.g. C04-30, C15-22, C13-30), and choosing by rank alone could drop public posts or pair a reserve with its neighbour. Reserves beside a topical neighbour (C04-30 with C04-29, C05-04 with C05-14, C07-22 with C07-03, C14-13 with C14-09) make different arguments from different key sources, so they can replace their neighbour or, within the two-per-cluster limit and with distinct wording, another post. C13-02 and C16-27 were removed as reserves because they repeat a selected argument. Verify early (support may rest partly on unopenable official text): C18-15 (Care Act s10(5) from an opened copy or a published paper), C18-22 (practical advice only), C18-14 (GMC confidentiality text), C03-09 (add Zalmay 2021; Scottish welfare attorney wording), C09-08 (capacity law and case law), C16-01 (add Finucane 2019), C16-26 (Winn 2023 or CHiP), C16-28 (six-week rule), C14-18 (wax removal access wording), C15-04 (Alqenae 2020), C15-07 (Fast Track is England-only), C06-08 (patch residue), C19-22 (rotigotine conversion), C07-12 (QRISK3 outputs at 78), C02-05 (1.2 m/s assumption), C17-07 (Schulz 2004 core; money rules optional). Delirium: twelve selected posts rest on studies that also report delirium outcomes (C01-28, C02-16, C03-06, C03-07, C03-17, C03-19, C06-08, C08-10, C08-17, C14-20, C15-12, C16-15); leave those findings out. Coherence for writers: each category's writer_guidance carries the check's wording and scheduling instructions. Also: word C19-04 and C19-28 consistently on home death; present C13-14 and C13-27 as associations with pneumonia, not proof; keep C14-09 on glasses between operations, not falls (C01-23 owns glasses and falls); C06-31 (a programme) and C06-32 (advice to patients) both involve NSAID combinations and should be scheduled apart; C08-03, C08-08 and C11-02 all mention donepezil in different roles; C16-12 must not read as fatalistic; C01-25 (fixed, unchanged) should not repeat the 'about a quarter' falls figure from earlier post E065 and should focus on telling classes apart.
